acceptance: each of the three cells runs its full matched denominator: 2 cases x 2 repeats = 4 episodes, all producing an outcome (success/failed/needs_clarification); an infrastructure_error is recorded with a named cause in errors.jsonl and counted as a miss against this item rather than dropped
privileged is the unchanged control: 4/4 on the matched denominator with the same budgets as E2'/E2'' (no repricing) and the same action sequence (11/11/13/13 rounds on c1/c3 repeat 0)

every failed episode names its residual cause, and the name is one of the three this stage ruled on: which of #25 (two-yellow ambiguity, ruled a structural limitation), #26 (intermittent detection, ruled a structural limitation) and #27 (the request ceiling, split and repriced by Q1) the episode actually died of. An episode whose cause cannot be named fails this item -- the naming is the harder criterion and the one SPEC §6 makes primary

the Q1 split is reported per episode: http_requests against perception_requests and decision_requests, with the unattributed remainder (the shared goal parse) shown rather than folded into either book

no episode dies on the HTTP ceiling unless the ledger shows the perception book as the book that filled it: the note text names the book, and a 'budget 48' note with an empty perception book is a defect of this batch, not a finding
RQ13's continuation is reported per cell on the matched denominator, side by side with E2'' (4/4, 0/4, 0/4) and E2' (4/4, 0/4, 0/4) and never merged with either
the per-episode rows carry both grounding_map_sha256 and the effective budgets, so a repriced cell is recognisable from its archive

budget_repricing.ruling: D2''' candidate B -- the per-episode request ceiling is batch configuration; D5''' set it at 48 total / 48 perception for the camera cells
budget_repricing.why_not_privileged: privileged makes zero requests (Q1's split measured 280 of 280 camera requests as looks and none as decisions), so repricing it would change a control's identity for no measurement; it therefore runs on the frozen budgets, exactly as in E2'/E2''
budget_repricing.why_both_at_48: the preflight checks the total before the perception book, so a total of 32 would still stop every camera episode at 32 and the perception cap of 48 would never be reached -- the repricing has to move the outer bound or it is decoration. The decision allowance is 0 because the rule policy spends none, which is the measured composition rather than a guess
budget_repricing.declared_identity_change: the budgets of the stub and vlm cells differ from E2'/E2''; the readers, the bridge and the frozen task table are untouched. Rows are reported side by side with both earlier batches and never pooled (SPEC §2.4)

spend_bound.basis: by composition after Q1: only the vlm cell spends, 4 episodes x the 48-request perception cap = 192 worst case, x1.25 head-room = 240. The SPEC's earlier 185 was priced against the pre-Q1 total of 32 and no longer holds (SPEC §7 principle 19: the bound follows the composition)
spend_bound.formula: episodes_that_spend x perception_cap + episodes_that_spend x decision_allowance, x1.25
spend_bound.stop_rule: 3 consecutive 429/quota errors -> stop the batch, save the checkpoint, log it; bound hit -> stop, no 'a little more'
spend_bound.stop_rule_source: v0.3 SPEC §8 verbatim, plus v0.4 §8 (endpoint rotation is an event, not a configuration)
spend_bound.resume: cell-level: a finished cell is never re-run; --resume continues a cell from its own checkpoint
